goal: Explain Causa's product value, evidence pipeline, causal RCA method, investigation workspace, guarded remediation model, and current production-readiness posture to engineering leaders, SRE teams, platform engineers, and technical evaluators.

deck_context.source_summary: Causa is an observability-driven root-cause analysis system for Kubernetes microservices. Alertmanager triggers a durable ingestion stage that scopes and snapshots Prometheus metrics, Tempo traces, Loki logs, topology, and infrastructure context. Stage 2 builds incident graphs, detects anomalies, isolates possible multi-fault incidents, ranks root-cause candidates, and persists explainable reports in Postgres. A React/FastAPI dashboard connects the RCA story to evidence, timelines, topology, related telemetry, feedback, and durable incident history. Remediation is proposal-first: typed plans pass through policy, human approval, leased workers, SLO observation, and rollback handling. Automatic execution remains blocked until calibration and operational readiness gates pass.
deck_context.core_claim: Causa compresses the path from alert to accountable action by connecting cross-signal evidence, influence-aware causal ranking, an operator investigation workspace, and guarded remediation without hiding uncertainty.

slides.title: Causal RCA — Rank Origins, Not the Loudest Symptoms
slides.intent: Explain how graph orientation, T/D/P scoring, arbitration, and isolation turn raw anomalies into explainable ranked origins.
key_points: Orient edges by failure influence.
Score temporal precedence, outward influence, and path consistency.
Promote infrastructure origins; isolate or abstain on multi-fault ambiguity.

local_context.required_background: Causa combines four graph views: infrastructure, service dependency, trace execution, and incident subgraph. For synchronous HTTP/gRPC/DB calls, failure influence reverses callee-to-caller; asynchronous producer-to-consumer flow is preserved; infrastructure runs-on edges point infrastructure-to-service. Candidate score is S(N) = wT·T(N) + wD·D(N) + wP·P(N), where T is temporal precedence, D is outward versus inward influence, and P is causal path consistency. Layer arbitration can promote an infrastructure origin above a hosted victim. Multi-fault isolation may separate incidents or abstain when ambiguous.

layout.composition: Technical before/after across the upper two-thirds: left is ordinary call direction, center is a bold transform arrow labeled failure influence, right is the oriented influence graph with one ranked origin. Along the bottom, a compact T/D/P score ribbon leads into arbitration and isolation outcomes.
layout.content_zones: Title top; before/after graph center; scoring ribbon and two outcome callouts bottom.
layout.relationship_to_previous_slide: Zoom-in from system architecture to the core reasoning mechanism.
layout.spacing: Moderate density with large readable graph labels and a compact equation.

visual_elements.main_visual: Before/after graph demonstrating that a downstream database sink in the call graph becomes an outward origin in the influence graph.

slides.title: Guarded Remediation — Automation With a Brake Pedal
slides.intent: Communicate that remediation is typed, policy-controlled, human-approved, observable, reversible where possible, and blocked from autonomy without evidence.
key_points: Typed immutable plan with exact target, fingerprint, risk, approvals, and SLO gates.
Human approval before a leased worker executes.
Observe live SLOs; succeed, fail safely, or roll back.
Automatic execution stays blocked until calibration gates pass.

local_context.required_background: Causa routes classified fault types into typed remediation plans. Supported actions include configuration patch, dependency rollback to a recorded last-good revision, scale/restart actions, data-path recovery, and draft code-fix PR. Plans carry exact targets, immutable fingerprints, risk tiers, required approvals, and SLO gates. Human approval precedes execution. Durable workers claim approved plans with leases and heartbeats, reject stale ownership, record an audit lifecycle, observe Prometheus SLOs, and trigger rollback handling. Automatic execution remains disabled without a validated non-constant calibration artifact and sufficient labeled incidents.

layout.composition: A large gated circular process: Propose → Policy → Human approval → Leased worker → Observe SLOs, then branch to Success or Rollback. A vertical safety ledger on the right lists plan invariants and the autonomy lock.

layout.relationship_to_previous_slide: Continue the operator journey from investigation into controlled action.
layout.spacing: Moderate density with a clear process path and one prominent amber approval gate.

slides.title: What Is Proven — and What Is Deliberately Gated
slides.intent: Balance demonstrated capability with an honest, decision-ready view of evaluation and production-readiness requirements.
key_points: Validated now
Required before autonomy

local_context.required_background: Validated in a controlled OpenTelemetry demo: the full path Prometheus → Alertmanager → causa-ingest → Stage 2 RCA → Postgres → dashboard API → UI; deterministic fixtures for a clear database cascade, infrastructure-rooted origin, disjoint dual faults, shared downstream dependency, and ambiguous near-simultaneous faults; durable remediation lease and rollback safety tests exist. Required before autonomy: a versioned labeled corpus spanning supported fault classes, alerts, and representative topology; disjoint training, calibration, and holdout incidents; at least 30 calibration incidents per automatically remediable action and holdout evidence; published top-1, top-3, MRR, abstention precision/recall, ECE, and time-to-diagnosis; clean baselines, representative alerts, fitted weights, validated calibration; operational controls including trusted-network restriction, dedicated roles, immutable images, backup/restore, lease-expiry drills, and surfaced rollback failure.

layout.composition: Two asymmetric evidence columns separated by a vertical gate: left blue/teal column titled Validated now with an end-to-end chain and five fixture badges; right amber/slate column titled Required before autonomy with Corpus, Calibration, Holdout metrics, and Operational controls. layout.content_zones: Title top; validated evidence left; readiness gates right; bottom posture bar.
